patterns.name: Binary contrasts
patterns.regex: (?:It['’]s not |The question isn[’]t |It[’]s not just )(.*?)\.(?: It[’]s Y| it[’]s Y| but Y)\.?
patterns.fix: State Y directly. "The eval matters more than the model."

patterns.name: Throat-clearing openers
patterns.regex: (?:Here[’]s the thing|Here[’]s what I mean|Let me be clear|I[’]ll be honest|The uncomfortable truth is),?\s*
patterns.example: "Here's the thing, the new platform is great."
patterns.fix: Cut the opener and state the point directly.

patterns.name: Faux-insight setups
patterns.regex: (?:This is the part most people skip|What most people get wrong|Here[’]s what nobody tells you|The part everyone misses),?\s*
patterns.example: "What nobody tells you is how hard it really is."
patterns.fix: Cut the setup and make the claim stand on its own.

patterns.name: Colon reveals
patterns.fix: Rewrite as plain sentence. "A separate agent does the grading, which is what makes it work."

patterns.name: Superficial analysis
patterns.example: "The launch adds file search, highlighting the team's commitment."
patterns.fix: Cut the -ing clause. "The launch adds file search, so users can find old drafts."

patterns.name: Importance puffery
patterns.regex: \b(stands as a testament|marks a pivotal moment|plays a vital role|solidifies its position|underscores its significance)\b
patterns.example: "The launch marks a pivotal moment for the company."
patterns.fix: State the fact. "The launch is the company's first paid product."

patterns.name: Weasel attribution
patterns.regex: \b(experts agree|industry reports suggest|many argue|widely regarded as|studies show)\b
patterns.fix: Name the source or cut the claim.

patterns.name: Synonym cycling
patterns.regex: (?:The agent reviews|The assistant scores|The tool suggests)\b
patterns.example: "The agent reviews the draft. The assistant scores the piece. The tool suggests fixes."
patterns.fix: Use clear word consistently. "The agent reviews the draft, scores it, and suggests fixes."

patterns.name: Negative listing
patterns.example: "Not a X. Not a Y. A Z."

patterns.name: Rhetorical setups
patterns.regex: (?:What if I told you|Think about it:|Plot twist:|\?\s+Answer:)\s*
patterns.example: "What if I told you this would change everything?"
patterns.fix: Drop and make the point directly.

patterns.name: Fake-profound kickers
patterns.regex: (?:In the end|At the end of the day|Truly|Fundamentally|Ultimately),\s*\w+\s+\w+\.$
patterns.example: "The future isn't coming. It's already here."
patterns.fix: Delete the kicker, end on the clearest concrete sentence.

patterns.name: Summary-recap endings
patterns.fix: End on the last concrete point, takeaway, or next action.

patterns.name: Formatting slop
patterns.example: Emoji in headings, bold sprinkled mid-sentence.
patterns.fix: Format should follow the content, not decorate it.

patterns.name: Em dashes
patterns.example: Multiple em dashes used as rhythm crutch.
patterns.fix: Use sparingly: none in short copy, 1-2 in longer drafts when they clearly help.

patterns.name: Fake-strong verbs
patterns.regex: \b(serves as a centralized hub for|acts as|serves as)\b
patterns.example: "The app serves as a centralized hub for sponsor management."
patterns.fix: Use direct description. "The app tracks sponsors, drafts, due dates, and approvals in one place."
